mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month signals a strengthening supply side, which can lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO rise > 1% does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand environment, which can lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).
